title.text: How to read a written form

phrase.text: A written form is the mould of a construct: it says which words are fixed, which slots you fill in and which parts you may leave out.

runs.text: A written form is the mould of a construct: it says which words are fixed, which slots you fill in and which parts you may leave out.
Every language construct is first shown with its form. Coloured words are written exactly as shown. Slots
are replaced by code. Whatever goes between ⟦ and ⟧ is optional: you may write it or not.
Below the form there is usually a

. You follow it like a railway track: left to right and top to bottom. Pills are fixed words; dashed boxes are slots; a track that passes underneath something means you may skip it, and a track that loops back means you may repeat it.

blocks.alt: How to follow a syntax diagram
blocks.description: Three strips of track. The first runs straight through the word While and the slot expression. The second has a detour that goes down to Else and back up, so Else can be skipped. The third passes through the slot statement and has a loop underneath back to the start, so the statement can be repeated.

caption.text: The three pieces of a syntax diagram: a fixed stretch, an optional detour and a loop for repeating.
